title: How to Prepare a Product Video Before Hiring
h1: How to prepare a product video before hiring
description: Prepare a product video: purpose, audience, key features, shots, sample product, script, formats, revisions and what to ask a product video creator.
intro: A product video shows what your product is, how it works and why someone should buy it. It can be filmed, animated or a mix of both, and it may live on a product page, in ads, on marketplaces or on social media. The best results come from a clear plan. This article explains what to decide and what to prepare before you hire a creator, so the video does its job and you pay for the right things.

faq.q: How long should a product video be?
faq.a: It depends on where it appears. Short clips of fifteen to thirty seconds suit ads and social feeds, while product pages can use a longer one that shows details.

faq.q: Do I need to send the product?
faq.a: For filmed videos, usually yes. For animation or 3D, files, drawings or clear photos may be enough.

faq.q: Should the video have a voice-over?
faq.a: Many viewers watch with sound off, so use captions and visuals that work without audio, and add voice or music as a bonus.

faq.q: Which formats should I ask for?
faq.a: Ask for the shapes your platforms use, such as vertical, square and widescreen versions, so that one video serves several places.

faq.q: What if my product changes later?
faq.a: Ask how easy it will be to update the video and whether source files are included.
